A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SelfMOTR work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v2 reports original tracking experiments on DanceTrack, BFT, AnimalTrack, and MOT17, together with component ablations and attention analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds decoder-sharing and detection-accuracy comparisons in Tables 5–6.

M1.justification: SelfMOTR retains the same shared-decoder detection and tracking passes, proposal construction, learned anchors, and training losses. The newly evaluated independent-decoder variant is an ablation control; the proposed method is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training and evaluation coverage, including DanceTrack, CrowdHuman, BFT, AnimalTrack, COCO pretraining, and appendix MOT17 experiments. The added comparisons use existing DanceTrack tasks and splits.

E2.justification: v3 adds TransTrack to the DanceTrack comparison in Table 2, although it already appeared in the animal benchmarks. Table 6 newly compares YOLOX and MOTRv2 against SelfMOTR on detection AP, and Table 5 introduces an independent-decoder control.

E3.justification: The new Table 5 evaluates independent versus shared decoder parameter sets on DanceTrack test, adding a model-configuration control. Previously stated training schedules, preprocessing, splits, metrics, and the appendix MOT17 clip-length experiment remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a targeted decoder weight-sharing ablation and an analysis comparing internal and external proposal detection accuracy and parameter counts. Existing query-interference, decoder-depth, threshold, data-scaling, and appendix analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Existing attention-distribution plots and their reporting remain unchanged, and the added tables introduce no uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are retained. New entries include TransTrack's 45.5 DanceTrack HOTA in Table 2, the independent decoder's 66.2 HOTA and 54.5 AssA versus SelfMOTR's retained 69.2 and 59.3 in Table 5, and validation AP of 79.7 for YOLOX and 75.3 for MOTRv2 in Table 6.

T1.justification: The proposal definitions, loss equations, cardinality-corrected Track-Attention Mass, and normalized entropy definition are unchanged. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about internal detection priors, reduced query interference, and competitive tracking. Headline results remain 69.2 HOTA on DanceTrack and 71.1 on BFT; the added evidence does not redefine the contributions.

C2.justification: v3 specifically interprets decoder sharing as improving association through alignment of proposal generation and track refinement. It also explains the detection, association, and parameter-count tradeoffs against YOLOX/MOTRv2. Existing MOT17 limitations and cross-domain attention interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: v3 newly discloses parameter counts of 42M for SelfMOTR, 99M for YOLOX, and 141M for the MOTRv2 pipeline. Figures 5–6 also identify the DanceTrack validation setting more explicitly. Existing hyperparameters and project/code access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands discussion of the already-cited TransTrack, explaining its separate decoders and IoU matching alongside TrackFormer's joint decoding. v3 adds a MOTChallenge reference. Most remaining bibliography changes correct metadata for existing sources.

P1.justification: v3 locally rewrites related work, adds discussion accompanying the new comparisons, updates author affiliations and correspondence, replaces placeholder running headers, and adds acknowledgements. The main section structure and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 5–6 and a TransTrack row in Table 2, refines Figure 3's copying/proposal annotations, and clarifies figure captions. Existing appendix Tables 5–7 become Tables 7–9. The overall format and existing plotted evidence are retained.

improvement.justification: Tables 5–6 strengthen the rationale for the existing shared decoder and make the detection-accuracy versus association and model-size tradeoffs more explicit. The added TransTrack comparison and expanded related-work discussion improve contextual coverage. These are useful, bounded gains; the core method, established results, and acknowledged limitations remain unchanged.
